• Checksum Type — The hash algorithm t:
• Checksum Type — The hash algorithm to use:
      – SHA-256: Strong, widely used. Recommended for general use.
      – SHA-1: Legacy but still common.
      – MD5: Fast but cryptographically weak. Fine for data integrity checks.
      – SHA-512: Strongest option. Slightly slower.
      – CRC32: Very fast but only a 32-bit check. Good for quick sanity checks.

  • Sector-by-sector comparison — Compares every sector individually (thorough but slower). Recommended.
  • Verify subchannel data — Also checks subchannel data stored alongside main sectors.
  • Audio track verification — When enabled, reads and verifies audio track data from the disc alongside data tracks. Essential for complete verification of mixed-mode CDs (e.g. PS1 games with audio tracks). When disabled, only data tracks are compared.
• Copy Speed — Speed at which to read:
• Copy Speed — Speed at which to read the disc. Lower speeds (e.g. 4x, 8x) improve accuracy on damaged or scratched discs at the cost of longer read times. Maximum speed is fastest but may produce errors on imperfect media.

  • Error Recovery — Controls what happens when a sector cannot be read:
      – Yes (skip and retry): Retry failed sectors a number of times, then skip
      – No (ignore errors): Read continues without retrying
      – Abort on error: Stop the entire read if any error occurs

  • Retry Count — Number of retry attempts for each failed sector (0–20). More retries can recover data from marginal sectors but increase read time.

  • Sector Size — Size of each sector in bytes:
      – 2048 bytes: Standard data sector size (suitable for most data discs)
      – 2352 bytes: Raw sector size (includes all error correction, sync patterns, and headers — required for audio CDs and accurate disc images)

  • Subchannel Mode — Controls extraction of subchannel data alongside main sectors:
      – None: No subchannel extraction (fastest, sufficient for most data discs)
      – Raw: Extract raw subchannel data (96 bytes per sector)
      – Other modes may be available depending on the disc type
      Subchannel data is essential for copy-protected discs and many gaming disc formats.

  • Audio Paranoia Mode — Extra error correction for audio CDs. Reads each sector multiple times and cross-references results to produce bit-perfect audio copies. Recommended for scratched or damaged audio CDs.

  • Jitter Correction — Corrects jitter (timing drift) during audio reading. Enabled by default. Helps ensure sample-accurate audio rips.

  • Read all sectors (including bad) — Forces the reader to attempt every sector on the disc, even those flagged as bad. Useful for forensic or archival purposes.

For raw BIN/CUE images, disc verificatio: For raw BIN/CUE images, disc verification uses READ CD (raw 2352-byte sectors) instead of READ(10). Each sector is individually classified by its sync pattern: sectors with the CD sync pattern are data (2048 bytes of user data extracted), sectors without sync are audio. When Audio Track Verification is enabled, audio sectors are hashed at the full 2352 bytes per sector. Both the disc side and image side use the exact same per-sector classification logic, ensuring consistent checksums regardless of CUE layout (single-file or multi-file) or pregap placement. On mixed-mode CDs, the 150-frame pregap between data and audio tracks is correctly handled: data ranges exclude the pregap (which contains audio-format sectors), and audio ranges include it when Audio Track Verification is enabled. If a sector read fails with the initial expected sector type, the engine retries with CD-DA type to recover pregap sectors near track boundaries. The disc visualization maps LBA positions to physical radius on the disc spiral (inner hub to outer edge).
